vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agentic-commerce-forthecult
Version: 1.0.3

The skill bundle provides agentic commerce capabilities, allowing an AI agent to browse products, create orders, and track shipments on forthecult.store. All API interactions are confined to the specified domain (https://forthecult.store/api). The SKILL.md documentation includes strong, explicit security guardrails for the AI agent, specifically instructing it not to follow URLs or endpoint paths from API responses (e.g., `error.suggestions` or `_actions`) that point to any other host or to undocumented paths. While the skill handles sensitive information like shipping addresses, email, and optional wallet addresses for discounts, and facilitates cryptocurrency payments, these actions are core to its stated purpose and are accompanied by explicit requirements for user confirmation and transparency regarding data usage. There is no evidence of intentional harmful behavior, data exfiltration to unauthorized parties, persistence mechanisms, or obfuscation.

llm.summary: The skill's declared purpose (autonomous shopping and multi-chain checkout) matches its instructions and requirements; it is an instruction-only integration that does not request extra credentials or installs, though there are a few privacy/operational notes to consider before use.

dimensions.detail: Name/description match the documented API endpoints and workflows in SKILL.md and the references. All required actions (search, product detail, checkout, order status) map to the API paths shown; multi-chain payments and optional wallet-based discounts are explained and justified by the store use case.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md is detailed and stays within commerce scope (search, checkout, tracking). Two notable instructional items: (1) it recommends calling /api/agent/me with X-Moltbook-Identity if the runtime supplies that header — which would expose the agent/runtime identity to forthecult.store; (2) it prescribes active polling (every 5s while awaiting_payment) and an auto-retry/auto-recovery pattern. Both are functionally reasonable for this commerce flow but have privacy and rate-limit implications and should only be used with explicit user consent and runtime policy controls.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — instruction-only skill. Nothing will be written to disk or downloaded as part of install, so installation risk is minimal.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials, which is proportional. However it optionally uses an X-Moltbook-Identity header if the runtime provides it, and it asks for user email, shipping address, and optionally a wallet address at checkout — these are user PII/financial data that will be sent to the third-party store. Requiring user consent before exposing runtime identity or the user's wallet/address is important.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true, does not declare config path access, and does not modify other skills. Default autonomous invocation is allowed (platform default) but is not combined with elevated privileges here.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent for autonomous shopping: it uses the store's public API and requires no extra credentials or installs. Before enabling or using it, consider the following: (1) do not forward your runtime/agent identity (X-Moltbook-Identity) to the store unless you trust forthecult.store and have explicit consent — that header exposes agent identity to a third party; (2) the skill will send user PII (email, shipping address) and optionally a wallet address to the store during checkout — get explicit user permission before transmitting; (3) crypto payments are irreversible — verify addresses and amounts with the user before instructing any transfers; (4) polling and auto-retry behavior is documented but may have rate-limit or privacy trade-offs — ensure your runtime enforces rate limits and logs appropriately; (5) the skill's source is listed as unknown in the registry metadata — if you need higher assurance, test in a sandbox account, confirm the HTTPS origin (https://forthecult.store) and contact the listed support email. If the runtime will automatically supply identity or wallet info without prompting, treat that as a policy/permission risk and restrict the skill until you can control those flows.
